chunks: And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās:

That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out to seek rain and said to al-ʿAbbās, “Stand and supplicate to your Lord and seek rain.” And he said, “O Allah, we seek a means to You through the uncle of Your Prophet.”

So al-ʿAbbās stood, praised Allah, and extolled Him. Then he said: “O Allah, indeed with You are clouds, and indeed with You is rain, so spread the clouds and send down water in it, then send it down upon us, strengthen thereby the roots, bring forth thereby the branches, and revive thereby the crops. O Allah, we are intercessors to You on behalf of those among our beasts and our cattle who have no speech; accept our intercession for ourselves and our families. O Allah, we call upon none but You, and we desire none but You. O Allah, give us a gentle, beneficial, all-covering, resounding rain. O Allah, we complain to You of the hunger of every hungry one, the nakedness of every unclothed one, the fear of every fearful one, and the hunger of every famished one who calls upon Allah.”

key_terms.سَقْيًا: a rainfall or watering from Allah
key_terms.شُفَعَاءُ: those pleading or interceding on behalf of others
key_terms.نَتَوَسَّلُ: we seek nearness or a means to Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the supplication for rain and seeking a means to Allah through al-ʿAbbās?
ai.summary: This report describes a prayer for rain in which al-ʿAbbās supplicates to Allah for relief from drought, hunger, and hardship. It emphasizes turning only to Allah in du'a, while seeking nearness through the uncle of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and includes concern for both people and animals.
